summary.intent: Run the GSD secure-phase workflow for Phase 44 (ipns-conflict-handling) to produce a verified SECURITY.md, then run a CodeRabbit CLI review of the phase-44 diff and apply all findings.
summary.outcome: Phase 44 SECURITY.md was created at the correct phase-scoped path with all 26 threats verified (19 mitigated, 7 accepted). CodeRabbit surfaced a critical data-loss bug in the file conflict merge path; all 4 findings were fixed, tested (196 tests pass), and committed.

repo: Branch feat/ipns-conflict-handling stacks phases 42, 43, and 44; phase-44-only base commit is 150db25d9 (20 files, ~1.5k lines).
dist/ is gitignored in sdk-core — build artifacts do not appear in git status.
The root SECURITY.md is the project's public GitHub vulnerability disclosure policy and must not be overwritten by phase audit artifacts.
Phase 44 was split into 7 sub-plans, each with a formal <threat_model> block, totalling 26 registered threats.

code.finding: Critical data-loss bug: mergeVersions() was passed remoteMeta.versions as the second arg in both branches. When remote wins, the loser is local metadata, so the second arg must be loser.versions — otherwise local version history is silently dropped and only the current CID survives.
With createVersion: false, loser.versions retains the full local history — this is the list that was being dropped by the bug above.

updatedMetadata.modifiedAt is overwritten to Date.now() before the winner comparison, so test fixtures must set remoteMeta.modifiedAt to a future timestamp (Date.now() + offset) to force the remote-wins branch — setting it to any value <= now() will make local win.

The remote-wins conflict test used empty local versions arrays, which masked the data-loss bug — the test only asserted the loser's current CID became a VersionEntry, not that prior version history was preserved.
is409() uses optional chaining throughout, so it safely returns false for null/undefined inputs without throwing — safe to unit-test with those values.

workflow: The gsd-security-auditor subagent writes its output to the repo-root SECURITY.md instead of the phase-scoped path; the orchestrator must detect and move the file after the subagent returns.
The GSD commit helper (gsd_run query commit) frequently returns commit_failed as a false-negative while the commit actually lands — always verify with git log before retrying.
CodeRabbit CLI (v0.5.4, auth as github/FSM1) supports --from <sha> to scope a review to a specific base commit, which is essential when multiple phases are stacked on one branch.

When the security auditor returns SECURED but a subsequent code review finds a bug in the mitigated area, the SECURITY.md threat entries that covered that area should be flagged as partially invalidated until the fix is committed.

friction: gsd-security-auditor wrote its phase audit report into the repo-root SECURITY.md (the public disclosure policy) instead of the phase-scoped path — required manual detection, git restore, and re-writing the file to the correct location.
GSD commit helper returned commit_failed on a commit that actually succeeded, requiring git log verification to avoid a double-commit.
First grep for is409 usages hit a shell glob expansion error and returned no results, requiring a corrected invocation.

Initial remote-wins test fixture was wrong: updatedMetadata.modifiedAt is overwritten to Date.now() internally, so the fixture accidentally produced a local-wins scenario — test passed for the wrong reason and required a second fixture fix.
open_items: 44-SECURITY.md threat entries T-44-09 and T-44-21 reference unit tests as mitigation evidence, but those tests were inadequate at audit time — the SECURITY.md audit trail should be updated to note the post-audit fix commit.

The gsd-security-auditor agent prompt/constraints should be patched to write phase audit output to the phase-scoped path rather than the repo root, to prevent recurrence across all future secure-phase runs.
is409 was omitted from the sdk-core barrel export despite the Phase 44 SUMMARY claiming it was re-exported — worth auditing other new exports in phases 42-44 for similar barrel gaps.
